title: The degree-zero part is compatible with base change
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
and let $k'/k$ be a field extension. Then the
base change of the
degree-zero part along
$\Spec(k')\to\Spec(k)$ is the degree-zero part of the base change:

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\times_k k'\;\cong\;\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'} .
$$

proof.text: *The base-changed curve satisfies the hypotheses.* $C_{k'}=C\times_kk'$ is again a smooth projective curve over $k'$ which is geometrically integral, so that [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] and [def-pd-degree-morphism] apply to it. Indeed, for a field extension $k''/k'$ the composite $k''/k$ is a field extension and $(C_{k'})_{k''}=C_{k''}$ by the transitivity of base change in [def-pc-base-change]; hence $C_{k'}$ is geometrically integral over $k'$ by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] (applied to $C$ over $k$), in particular integral. The structure morphism $C_{k'}\to\Spec(k')$ is separated, of finite type and smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1)-(2) and projective by [lem-pc-projective-base-change], and $\dim C_{k'}=1$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change]; so $C_{k'}$ is a smooth projective curve over $k'$ in the sense of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve].

By [lem-pd-picard-base-change] the functor
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ restricts to
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C_{k'}/k'}$ on the slice over $k'$, and the restriction of
a functor to a slice is the base change in the sense of
[def-pc-base-change]. The degree morphism of
[def-pd-degree-morphism] is defined through the fibrewise degree of [def-pd-fibrewise-degree], and the two fibrewise degrees agree on the slice: for $T$ over $k'$ one has $(C_{k'})_T=C_T$ and, for $t\in T$, the fibre $(C_{k'})_{\kappa(t)}=C_{\kappa(t)}$ over the same field $\kappa(t)$ ([def-pc-base-change]), so the fibrewise degree of an invertible module on $C_T$ computed for $C_{k'}$ over $k'$ is, by its definition, the one computed for $C$ over $k$. Hence the restriction of
$\deg:\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\to\underline{\Z}$ to the slice is the degree morphism of
$C_{k'}$ (the constant sheaf $\underline{\Z}$ restricts to the constant sheaf, both having value the locally constant functions $T\to\Z$). Restricting the kernel of a morphism of sheaves to a slice gives
the kernel of the restricted morphism (kernels are computed objectwise), so the two degree-zero parts agree after
base change, which is the displayed isomorphism.
